summary: Hardin County tower, about 100 ft; a courthouse-cupola lookout came first; a 1984 note says it was torn down in 1980; listed gone.

facts.design: Four-legged steel frame with a seven-foot square observation cage and pyramidal roof
facts.status_note: Torn down in 1980, according to a 1984 survey recovery note; no source describes the site today.

staffing.status: Lookout station in the courthouse cupola in 1926; lookout at the 100-foot tower in 1943

events.note: Lookout station maintained in the Hardin County courthouse cupola, elevation about 80 ft
Newspaper item says the cupola lookoutman discovered more than fifty fires in one fall season
Newspaper item names Mrs. N.D. Bartlett as lookout at the 100-foot glassed-in tower
Coast and Geodetic Survey station described: 100 ft overall, on state-owned property
Tower torn down during 1980, according to a 1984 recovery note
Survey station recovery: station destroyed, lookout tower no longer exists

corrections.why: The page heading reads Hardin County, Texas Forest Service; the record value is a stray comma.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1926 report gives the cupola an elevation of about 80 feet; the 1927 newspaper says about 85 feet from the ground. The story gives both figures.
The 1943 item says five miles southwest; the 1952 survey says about 4.0 miles west-southwest. The sources do not say which is more exact; the story gives both.

notes_for_editor: The NGS 1952 description (PID BL2102), the 1984 recovery note and the newspaper quotes (1927 Tulia Herald, 1943 Kerrville Times) are as transcribed on the centraluslookouts pages; originals not checked. The 1980 demolition date is second-hand in the 1984 note. No source found for when the tower was built. Record agency was a stray comma and is corrected. Story omits the family detail in the 1943 item.
